hints: Focus on what excess acidified dichromate under reflux does to primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols.
Remember that a primary alcohol gives a carboxylic acid, a secondary alcohol gives a ketone, and a tertiary alcohol shows no reaction.
Compare hydrogen bonding in the products: think about which product loses the ability to hydrogen bond and so will boil at a lower temperature than its alcohol.
walkthrough:
**Classify the oxidation outcome**

Great start, let's sort out what Q can be. Primary alcohols are oxidised fully to carboxylic acids under reflux with excess oxidant. Secondary alcohols are oxidised to ketones. Tertiary alcohols are not oxidised.

Rule:
$$\text{primary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{carboxylic acid}, \quad \text{secondary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{ketone}, \quad \text{tertiary alcohol} \rightarrow \text{no reaction}$$

**Link product type to boiling point**

Now think about intermolecular forces. Alcohols and carboxylic acids can hydrogen bond, but ketones cannot donate hydrogen bonds.

This means a carboxylic acid has a higher boiling point than its parent alcohol, while a ketone has a lower boiling point than its parent alcohol.

**Find the alcohol that gives a lower boiling product**

We need Q to boil lower than P, so Q must be a ketone. That means P must be a secondary alcohol.

$\text{pentan-2-ol}$ is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, a secondary alcohol, so it oxidises to pentan-2-one, which cannot hydrogen bond and boils lower.

options.A: 2-methylbutan-1-ol is a primary alcohol ($-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$). With excess reflux it gives 2-methylbutanoic acid, a carboxylic acid with stronger hydrogen bonding (dimer formation), so Q has a higher boiling point than P.
options.B: 2-methylbutan-2-ol is a tertiary alcohol with no hydrogen on the carbon bearing the $\text{OH}$ group. It is resistant to oxidation, so no Q is formed under these conditions.
options.C: Pentan-1-ol is a primary alcohol. It oxidises fully to pentanoic acid under reflux with excess dichromate. Carboxylic acids boil higher than alcohols, so Q would have a higher boiling point, opposite to what is observed.
options.D: Pentan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol. It oxidises to the ketone pentan-2-one. The ketone cannot form hydrogen bonds as a donor, so its intermolecular forces are weaker (dipole-dipole only) and its boiling point is lower than the parent alcohol. This matches perfectly.
